_about: Field terms for F210, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

luneburg-lens.definition: a sphere, or in two dimensions a cylinder, whose refractive index falls from the square root of 2 at the centre to 1 at the surface, so that a plane wave from any direction is focused to a point on the opposite surface
luneburg-lens.excludes: a uniform ball lens, and modified profiles whose focus lies inside or outside the surface

gradient-index.definition: describing an optical element whose refractive index changes smoothly through the material, so that light bends inside it along curved paths
gradient-index.excludes: a conventional lens of one material, which bends light only at its surfaces

partial-wave.definition: describing a solution in which the field around a round object is written as a sum of angular orders, each order is solved along the radius alone, and the orders are added up
partial-wave.excludes: ray tracing, which follows paths and carries no wavelength, and grid methods that sample the whole field

focal-peak.definition: the largest intensity found on the rear surface of the lens within the arc examined, reported as a share of the same quantity for the continuous lens of the same size
focal-peak.excludes: the total power delivered, the gain of an antenna, and any peak that forms off the rear surface
